drugs.moa: Stimulates beta-2 receptors to relax bronchial smooth muscle and open airways quickly.
nursing: It's a RESCUE inhaler for acute symptoms
Overuse can signal poor asthma control
teaching: Use it first, then wait a few minutes before the steroid inhaler
Report needing it more than usual
drugs.tip: Albuterol = RESCUE (SABA). Use BEFORE the steroid inhaler. Side effects: tremor, tachycardia.

drugs.moa: Reduces airway inflammation over time to prevent asthma symptoms — a controller, not a rescue drug.
adverse: Rare systemic effects with high doses
nursing: It's a daily CONTROLLER, not for acute attacks
Rinse the mouth after each use to prevent thrush
Use a spacer to improve delivery
teaching: Use every day, even when you feel well
Rinse and spit after each use
This will not stop a sudden attack
drugs.tip: Inhaled steroids = CONTROLLER (daily). Rinse mouth after use → prevents oral thrush. Not for acute attacks.

drugs.moa: Blocks acetylcholine in the airways, causing bronchodilation.
nursing: Not a first-line rescue drug (slower onset)
Avoid getting spray in the eyes
Good oral care for dry mouth
teaching: Keep spray out of your eyes
drugs.tip: Ipratropium: anticholinergic → dry mouth. "Can't see, can't pee, can't spit, can't poop" anticholinergic effects.
